Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR FUSE BOX FOR AUTOMOBILES

( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 25 August 1982, after the draft finalized by the Automotive ElecJrical Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1967. The present revision has been undertaken to update the contents, and to introduce various environmental tests and the endurance test. 0.3 This standard is intended to cover the requirements Bnd methods of tests for fuse box for use in automobile wiring and equipment. 0.4 In view of the importance. of achieving interchangeability, this standard lays down dimensions also, in addition to the performance requirements and methods of tests. 0.5 Fuse links conforming to the following with the fuse box specified in this standard: IS : 2577-1974
IS :

are suitable for use

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. *Rules for roundingoff numerical values ( rruired ). 3

I6 : 4063 - 1982 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements and methods of tests for fuse box for use in automobile wiring and equipment. 1.2 The fuse box is suitable for use with fuse links conforming IS : 2577-l 974* or IS : 752% 1974t. 2. TERMINOLOGY 20 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall to

apply*
that the fuselinks used in the fuse box, will carry continuously without deterioration in accordance with this standard.

2.1Rated Current - The current stated by the manufacturer

2.2Type Tests - Tests

carried out to prove conformity with the specification. These are intended to prove the general qualities and design of a given type of fuse box. 2.3 Acceptance Tests - Tests carried out on the samples taken from a lot for the purpose of acceptance of the lot. 2.4 Routine Tests - Tests carried out on each fuse box to check requirements which are likely to vary during production. 3. MATERIAL AND CONSTRUCTION

body or base of the fuse box shall be made of 3.1 Material -The non-conductive material, which shall be non-inflammable, nonhygroscopic, and unbreakable under normal use. The screw holes in the moulding may be reinforced, if necessary, with metal inserts. 3.1.1 All threaded metal inserts provided withstand a tightening torque of 10 Nm. in the moulding shall

3.2The holder clips shall be made of good conductivity material like
phospher bronze, brass or steel, suitably hardened to have sprtng quality, and suitably plated to protect against corrosion.

3.7 The fuse box may be provided with a suitable cover of noninflammable material and the cover shall be so fitted as to permit easy removal and fitment. In fitted condition there shall be minimum 3 mm If required by the purchaser, clearance between the clips and the cover. the cover shall be of suitable transparent material, in which case it shall be properly marked with the terminal locations. 4. Routine Tests -

5.2 Visual Examination and Dimensional Check - The fuse box shall be examined for fitment dimensions and finish. They shall show no They signs of cracks, burrs and other unwanted protruding materials. shall conform to the requirement in 3.3 and 3.4. 5.3 Millivolt Drop Test -The appropriate fuse link shall be mounted in the fuse box and a current equal to 50 percent of the rated capacity shall be passed. The millivolt drop when measured between the holder clip and the fuse cap .shall not be more than 1.5 millivolt per ampere. 9

IS : 4663 - 1982 5.4 Fuse Link Insertion/Extraction Test

5.4.1 A fuse link of the same rated current as the fuse holder shall be used to measure the force required to insert it into and then extract from the holder:

a) For cartridge fuse-links the force of insertion shall not exceed 50 N and shall not be less than 15 N. The force of extraction shall be within the limits of 15 N and 35 N. b) For porcelain ( moulded ) fuse-links the force of insertion shall not exceed 15 N and shall not be less than 10 N. The force of extraction shall be within the limits of 15 N and 35 N. 5.4.2 The insertion and extraction shall be repeated 30 times and clips shall not show any weakening of the insertion and extraction forces. 5.4.3 After the test the fuse box shall satisfy the requirements millivolt drop test ( 5.3 ). of

5.5 High Voltage Temt - The fuse box shall be subjected to an ac voltage of 240 V rms at a convenient frequency between 40 and 60 .Hz for a period of 1 minute between any terminal post and metal inserts for mounting screw). The fuse box shall satisfactorily withstand this teSt without arcing or puncture. 5.6 Vibration Test - The fuse box with fuse link in position, after being rigidly mounted on a suitable vibrating machine constructed to produce simple harmonic motion shall be subjected to vibrate (a total lift of 0.75 mm) through a frequency range of 10-55-10 Hz in a period of With continuously varying frequencies, the vibration shall one minute. be applied for not less than one hour in each of the three major axes of the box, At the end of the vibration test the fuse boxshall be examined for any evidence of damage and shall satisfy the requirement of the fuse link insertion/extraction test (5.4) and millivolt drop test (5.3). according to 5.7 Dry Heat Test - The tent shall be conducted IS : 9000 (Part III/Set 3).1977*. The test chamber temperature shall be 85�C and the duration of exposure shall be 4 hours. The fuse box shall be fitted with an appropriate fuse link during the test. 5.7.1 After the tect the fure box shall be examined diatorrion of shape and shall satisfy the requirement8 ta8t ( see 5.2 ). for any crack or of millivolt drop

ISt4063-1382 5.8 Cold Test - The test shall be conducted according to IS : 9000 (part II/Set 3)-1977*. The test chamber temperature shall be - 10�C and the duration of exposure shall be 2 hours. The fuse box shall be fitted with an appropriate fuse link during the test. 5.8.1 After the test the fuse box shall be examined for any crack or distortion of shape and shall satisfy the requirements of the millivolt drop test ( 5.3 ). 3.9 Damp Heat ( Cycling ) Test - The test shall be conducted as The number of conditioning specified in IS : 9000 (Part V/Set 2)-1981*. cycler shall be 7. 5.9.1 After the test the fuse box shall show no sign of corrosion, deterioration or damage and shall satisfy the requirements of millivolt drop test ( 3.3 ). 3.10 Change of Temperature Test according to IS : 9000 (Part XIV)-1978*. 5.10.1 The temperature The test shall be conducted

5.10.2 At the end of this test the fuse box shall show no sign of damage and shall pass millivolt drop test (5.3). 5.11 Dust Test - The fuse box shall be mounted in its normal operating position 150 mm from the wall in a box measuring 900 mm in all directions, containing 5 kg of fine powdered cement conforming to IS : 269-19767. At intervals of 15 minutes, this dust shall be agitated using compressed air or fan blower, by projecting blasts of air for a twosecond period in a downward direction into the dust in such a way that the dust shall be completely and uniformly diffused throughout the entire cube. The dust is then allowed to settle. This test shall be continued for 5 hours. *Specification for basic environmental testing procedures for electronic and electrical items: Part II Cold test, Section 3 Cold test for non heat dissipatingitems with gradual change oftemperature.

Resistance Test - The fuse box shall be sprayed with contaminents like diesel, petrol, thinner, lubricating oil and break fluid. The fuse box shall neither react with nor dissolve in the contaminents. 5.14 Contamination 5.15 Drop Test - The test shall be carried out as specified in IS : 9000 ( Part VII/Set 3 )-1979t. The fuse box shall be dropped 6 times in different orientations from a minimum height of 300 mm. There shall be no damage or distortion of parts.

5.16 Endurance Test - The fuse box shall be fitted with an appropriate fuse link. A current equal to 110 percent of the rated current The test may be carried out at any shall be passed for 1 000 hours. convenient voltage. The test current shall be maintained within f 2 percent during the test. The minimum duration of continuous run of the test There shall be no failure during shall be not less than 30 minutes. the test. 5.16.1 After the test the fuse box shall be tested for millivolt drop test ( 5.3 ). The value of millivolt drop shall not be more than 2.0 millivolt per ampere.

APPENDIX ( Clause 5.13 )

A

TEST FOR CORROSION RESISTANCE A-l. PROCEDURE
corrosion due to atmospheric test.

A-l.0 The ability of the fuse box with fuses in position, to withstand

conditions shall be assessed by the following

for this test shall be so constructed that the salt spray is produced in the lower part of the chamber, in the upper part of which the parts to be exposed are suspended.

A-l.1 The chamber

A-l.2 The spray shall be produced by an atomiser employing compressed
air free from all impurities.

A-l.3 The ceiling, the walls and all other parts of the chamber
so constructed and the parts under test so arranged can drip on the test specimen.

shall be that no condensate

A-l.4 The salt solution shall be a 5 percent solution of sodium chloride in water. A-l.5 The device shall be sprayed in such a chamber at the standard temperature of 27'%, for 50 hours consisting of two periods of 24 hours each and one hour drain.

A-l.6 After removal from the salt spray chamber,
show any sign of corrosion or electrolytic action.

the parts

shall not

A-l.7 In general, a salt spray chamber shown in Fig. 4 with a spraying arrangements as shown in Fig. 5 and complying with the following requirements would be suitable.

4

The cabinet should approximately be of the dimensions shown, and the cabinet and its internal fittings should be made of monel metal or any other suitable material. A shelf is required, which should be capable of being fitted in the upper or lower part of the cabinet; The air used for atomizing the salt solution shall be clean. The pressure during the tests shall be between 29 and 35 kKa. The pressure may be adjusted by a relief valve or by the pressure outlet of the blower; 13

b)

IS : 4063 - 1982 The nozzle for atomizing the salt solution shall be adjusted for maximum amount of spray. This adjustment may be carried out by unscrewing the bottom lock nut B, on the lower nozzle C, and adjusting this nozzles into position until maximum spray occurs. The diameter of the nozzle shall be l-5 mm. A tap and second branch in the air line is available for agitating the salt solution as required; The spraying apparatus shall be capable of atomizing not less than 1 450 ml salt solution per hour. The quantity of solution sprayed per cubic metre capacity of the test chamber shall be approximately 177 ml per minute; and The container filled with cotton wool acts as a breather and provides an outlet for the air which is constantly being pumped into the chamber, the cotton wool acting as a filter and preventing salt mist from being discharged into the atmosphere.
